sections.h2: What is the Marlboro, NJ housing market like for a seller?
sections.html:
Marlboro Township is a high-income Monmouth County suburb where owners occupy 93.1 percent of homes, so nearly every sale starts with a homeowner rather than a landlord. The Census Bureau's 2020 to 2024 survey puts median home value at $701,200, median household income at $186,292 and median gross rent at $2,699. The township's estimated population was 42,254 in mid-2025.

Households average 2.89 people, 23.4 percent of residents are under 18 and 17.9 percent are 65 or older. About 24.8 percent were born abroad and 31.8 percent speak a language other than English at home. Retirement communities in town include Greenbriar North, with more than 750 homes, and Marlboro Greens, with 341 homes built from 1986 to 1988.

sections.h2: How is Marlboro Township laid out?
sections.html:
Marlboro covers 30.34 square miles of land in the Raritan Valley region, and its neighborhoods read as scattered villages rather than a single downtown. The legislature formed it on February 17, 1848, from part of Freehold Township and named it for the marl beds in its soil. Morganville (6,203 residents in 2020) and Robertsville (11,399) are the two census-designated places, and Wickatunk, Pleasant Valley, Spring Valley and Montrose are among the other names on local maps.

A few details shape how houses present:

  • The Monmouth County Agricultural Railroad once ran through town with stops at Bradevelt, Marlboro, Morganville and Wickatunk, and its right of way is now a county rail trail.
  • In 1958 the township set aside 1,500 acres off Vanderburg Road for the Marlboro Industrial Park.
  • Average rainfall is about 47 inches a year, with about 23 inches of snow and some 179 freezing days.

Neighbors include Aberdeen, Colts Neck, Freehold Township, Holmdel, Manalapan and Matawan in Monmouth County, and Old Bridge in Middlesex County.

sections.h2: What does Marlboro require before a house is sold?
sections.html:
Marlboro Township requires a Continued Certificate of Occupancy for every home sale or rental. The Zoning/Code Enforcement Division issues it, and the paperwork is available on the township website or at the zoning office. Reach the zoning officer at 732-536-0200, extension 1809, on weekdays between 8:30 and 4:30.

Items behind a Marlboro Continued Certificate of Occupancy. Source: Marlboro Township Zoning/Code Enforcement FAQ.

Heating and coolingForm completed by an HVAC company
FireplaceInspection by a certified chimney sweep company
Well and septicCertification from the Monmouth County Board of Health
ApplicationFill out completely and circle sale or rental

Validity90 days from issue
Re-inspection$75 each

Before booking the inspection, ask the zoning office whether permits for sheds, fences, patios and decks are closed. A shed under 200 square feet needs a zoning permit with a scaled survey, and larger or wired sheds also need construction permits. Day to day, the division works from complaints, so a missing permit tends to come up when someone asks.

sections.h2: Do environmental records matter when selling a Marlboro house?
sections.html:
They can, because Marlboro's history includes contaminated sites that buyers and their lenders sometimes ask about. Wikipedia's township entry reports that the state environmental department lists 39 known locations in Marlboro with underground storage tank contamination. It also describes the Burnt Fly Bog Superfund cleanup site, about 1,700 acres off Tyler Lane and Spring Valley Road on the Old Bridge border, where waste oil was stored in lagoons in the 1950s and early 1960s.

For an owner, the practical step is to know what is buried or stored on the lot. Find out whether an old heating oil tank was removed or left in place, and keep any closure paperwork where a buyer can see it. For a house near the Spring Valley Road area, ask the zoning office for the block and lot file and the state environmental department for site records before a buyer's attorney asks.

sections.h2: What will the state and county charge when a Marlboro sale closes?
sections.html:
The seller pays New Jersey's realty transfer fee at recording, and a sale at Marlboro's median value of $701,200 comes to about $6,258 on the state schedule. Prices above $1,000,000 add a graduated percent fee, starting at 1 percent of the whole price, and the law has charged it to the seller since July 10, 2025.

Deeds are recorded by the Monmouth County Clerk, whose record room is at the Market Yard, 33 Mechanic Street in Freehold, open weekdays until 4:00 in the afternoon. The clerk's fee page lists $40 for the first page of a deed and $10 for each additional page. The seller's residency form (GIT/REP) is filed with the deed, and a signer who lives out of state may owe estimated income tax on the gain, which the form is designed to determine.

sections.h2: How do roads, trains and schools affect buyers in Marlboro?
sections.html:
Marlboro is a driving town: U.S. Route 9, Route 18, Route 79 and County Road 520 are the main thoroughfares, with Route 34 in the northeast corner. The township has 229.71 miles of road, most of it township-maintained. NJ Transit buses 131, 135 and 139 run to the Port Authority Bus Terminal in Manhattan. The nearest commuter rail stop is Aberdeen-Matawan on the North Jersey Coast Line. Workers average 41.2 minutes to get to their jobs.

Public schools through eighth grade belong to the Marlboro Township Public School District, which ran eight schools and enrolled 4,537 students in 2022 to 2023. Marlboro High School, part of the Freehold Regional High School District, had 1,816 students that year, and some Marlboro students attend Colts Neck High School instead. Private options in or near town include High Point Schools, Shalom Torah Academy and Christian Brothers Academy in Lincroft.

sections.h2: What are the ways to sell a Marlboro house fast?
sections.html:
Marlboro owners choose among a listing agent, a do-it-yourself sale and a cash buyer who accepts the house with its flaws. All three require the Continued Certificate of Occupancy, so the real differences are speed, cost and how much repair work the owner takes on.

  • An agent listing exposes the house to the most buyers and works well for a move-in ready property, although commissions and requested repairs reduce what the owner nets.
  • A sale without an agent keeps the commission while shifting pricing, showings and negotiation to the owner.
  • A cash purchase can fit an inherited house, a vacant property, or a house with an old oil tank or unpermitted work that would complicate a mortgage-financed buyer.

Put in writing who orders the HVAC form, the chimney inspection and the well or septic certification, and who pays for any fix the inspector requires.

faqs.q: Does Marlboro require an inspection when I sell my house?
faqs.a: Yes. Marlboro Township requires a Continued Certificate of Occupancy for every home sale or rental, issued after an inspection. It is good for 90 days, and each re-inspection costs $75.

faqs.q: What paperwork do I need from outside contractors for a Marlboro sale?
faqs.a: An HVAC company fills out the heating and cooling form, a certified chimney sweep inspects any fireplace, and a house on a well or septic system needs certification from the Monmouth County Board of Health.

faqs.q: How much is the realty transfer fee on a Marlboro home?
faqs.a: It depends on price and falls on the seller. At the Census median home value of $701,200 the state schedule comes to roughly $6,258, and sales above $1,000,000 also pay a graduated percent fee.

faqs.q: Where is a Marlboro deed recorded?
faqs.a: The Monmouth County Clerk records it, at the Market Yard, 33 Mechanic Street, Freehold. The clerk's fee page lists $40 for the first page of a deed and $10 per added page, with the transfer fee due at recording.

faqs.q: Should I worry about an old oil tank on my Marlboro property?
faqs.a: Yes, check it before listing. The state environmental department lists 39 underground storage tank contamination locations in Marlboro, so a buyer's attorney is likely to ask whether a tank was removed and whether closure records exist.
